content: After rising from the dead, for how many days did Jesus appear to His apostles?
explanation: He spoke about the kingdom of God. “He appeared to them over a span of forty days” (Acts 1:3, BSB)

content: Before going up to heaven, which city did Jesus tell His apostles not to leave?
explanation: They were to wait for the Father's gift. “Do not leave Jerusalem, but wait for the gift the Father promised” (Acts 1:4, BSB)

content: Before going up to heaven, Jesus said His apostles would soon be baptized with what?
explanation: John had baptized with water. “in a few days you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.” (Acts 1:5, BSB)

content: Before going up to heaven, what did Jesus say His apostles would receive when the Spirit came?
explanation: They would be His witnesses. “But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes upon you” (Acts 1:8, BSB)

content: Before going up to heaven, how far did Jesus say His witnesses would go?
options: To the ends of the earth
explanation: The good news is for everyone. “and to the ends of the earth.” (Acts 1:8, BSB)

content: As Jesus was taken up into heaven, what hid Him from the apostles' sight?
explanation: They watched Him go up. “they watched as He was taken up, and a cloud hid Him from their sight.” (Acts 1:9, BSB)

content: After Jesus went up to heaven, what did the two men in white promise?
options: He will come back the same way
explanation: Jesus will return. “will come back in the same way you have seen Him go into heaven.” (Acts 1:11, BSB)

content: On which feast day were the believers all together when the Holy Spirit came?
explanation: They were in one place. “When the day of Pentecost came, they were all together in one place.” (Acts 2:1, BSB)

content: On the day of Pentecost, what sound came from heaven and filled the house?
explanation: The Holy Spirit was coming. “Suddenly a sound like a mighty rushing wind came from heaven” (Acts 2:2, BSB)

content: On the day of Pentecost, what came to rest on each believer?
explanation: It was a sign of the Spirit. “They saw tongues like flames of fire that separated and came to rest on each of them.” (Acts 2:3, BSB)

content: On the day of Pentecost, after being filled with the Spirit, what did the believers do?
explanation: The Spirit enabled them. “began to speak in other tongues as the Spirit enabled them.” (Acts 2:4, BSB)

content: On the day of Pentecost, why was the crowd in Jerusalem amazed?
explanation: People came from every nation. “because each one heard them speaking his own language.” (Acts 2:6, BSB)

content: On the day of Pentecost, which apostle stood up and spoke to the crowd?
explanation: He stood with the Eleven. “Then Peter stood up with the Eleven, lifted up his voice, and addressed the crowd” (Acts 2:14, BSB)

content: About how many people were baptized after Peter's sermon at Pentecost?
explanation: They embraced his message. “about three thousand were added to the believers that day.” (Acts 2:41, BSB)

content: In the first church in Jerusalem, what did the believers devote themselves to?
explanation: These were the habits of the first church. “They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer.” (Acts 2:42, BSB)

content: How did the first believers in Jerusalem treat what they owned?
explanation: They cared for one another. “All the believers were together and had everything in common.” (Acts 2:44, BSB)

content: In the first church, why did believers sell their possessions?
options: To share with anyone in need
explanation: No one was left in need. “they shared with anyone who was in need.” (Acts 2:45, BSB)

content: In the first church in Jerusalem, how often did believers meet in the temple courts?
explanation: They broke bread in their homes too. “With one accord they continued to meet daily in the temple courts” (Acts 2:46, BSB)

content: Where did the first believers break bread together?
explanation: They shared meals with gladness. “and to break bread from house to house” (Acts 2:46, BSB)

content: In the first church, who added to their number daily?
explanation: Salvation is God's work. “And the Lord added to their number daily those who were being saved.” (Acts 2:47, BSB)

content: In the first church, what came over everyone as the apostles did wonders?
explanation: God was at work among them. “A sense of awe came over everyone” (Acts 2:43, BSB)

content: At which temple gate did the man lame from birth sit and beg?
explanation: He was put there every day. “the temple gate called Beautiful” (Acts 3:2, BSB)

content: Who was going up to the temple with Peter when they met the lame man?
explanation: It was the hour of prayer. “One afternoon Peter and John were going up to the temple at the hour of prayer” (Acts 3:1, BSB)

content: What did the lame man at the temple gate ask Peter and John for?
explanation: He begged every day. “he asked them for money.” (Acts 3:3, BSB)

content: What did Peter say he did not have to give the lame man?
explanation: He gave something better. “Silver or gold I do not have, but what I have I give you” (Acts 3:6, BSB)

content: In whose name did Peter tell the lame man to get up and walk?
explanation: The power was Jesus', not Peter's. “In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, get up and walk!” (Acts 3:6, BSB)

content: How did Peter help the lame man at the temple gate up?
options: Took him by the right hand
explanation: At once his feet grew strong. “Taking him by the right hand, Peter helped him up” (Acts 3:7, BSB)

content: After Peter healed him, what did the lame man do in the temple courts?
explanation: He was full of joy. “walking and leaping and praising God.” (Acts 3:8, BSB)

content: When the church chose seven helpers, who was described as full of faith and the Holy Spirit?
explanation: He was the first named of the seven. “They chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit” (Acts 6:5, BSB)

content: Stephen, one of the seven chosen helpers, was full of grace and what else?
explanation: He did great wonders and signs. “Now Stephen, who was full of grace and power” (Acts 6:8, BSB)

content: Before he was stoned, whom did Stephen see standing at God's right hand?
explanation: He saw heaven open. “I see heaven open and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God.” (Acts 7:56, BSB)

content: When Stephen was stoned, at whose feet did the witnesses lay their garments?
explanation: Saul later became Paul. “the witnesses laid their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.” (Acts 7:58, BSB)

content: While he was being stoned, what did Stephen pray?
explanation: He trusted Jesus to the end. “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.” (Acts 7:59, BSB)

content: What did Stephen ask God about the people who were stoning him?
options: Do not hold this sin against them
explanation: He forgave like Jesus did. “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” (Acts 7:60, BSB)

content: What broke out against the church on the day Stephen died?
explanation: The believers were scattered. “On that day a great persecution broke out against the church in Jerusalem” (Acts 8:1, BSB)

content: Who told Philip to go to the desert road toward Gaza?
explanation: God had someone for him to meet. “Now an angel of the Lord said to Philip, “Get up and go south to the desert road” (Acts 8:26, BSB)

content: On the desert road to Gaza, whom did Philip meet?
explanation: He was in charge of a queen's treasury. “on his way he met an Ethiopian eunuch, a court official” (Acts 8:27, BSB)

content: Which prophet was the Ethiopian official reading in his chariot?
explanation: He was returning from worship. “was sitting in his chariot reading Isaiah the prophet.” (Acts 8:28, BSB)

content: What did Philip ask the Ethiopian official reading in his chariot?
options: Do you understand what you're reading?
explanation: The official needed a guide. ““Do you understand what you are reading?” Philip asked.” (Acts 8:30, BSB)

content: The Ethiopian official read a scripture about someone led like what to the slaughter?
explanation: Philip explained it was about Jesus. “He was led like a sheep to the slaughter” (Acts 8:32, BSB)

content: When they came to some water, what did Philip do for the Ethiopian official?
explanation: The official believed the good news. “Then both Philip and the eunuch went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.” (Acts 8:38, BSB)

content: After his baptism, how did the Ethiopian official go on his way?
explanation: He had found the good news. “but went on his way rejoicing.” (Acts 8:39, BSB)

content: To which city was Saul traveling to arrest followers of Jesus?
explanation: He carried letters from the high priest. “and requested letters to the synagogues in Damascus” (Acts 9:2, BSB)
tags: Saul on the Road to Damascus

content: On the road to Damascus, what suddenly flashed around Saul?
explanation: Jesus was about to speak to him. “suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him.” (Acts 9:3, BSB)
tags: Saul on the Road to Damascus

content: On the road to Damascus, what did the voice from heaven ask Saul?
explanation: Hurting believers was hurting Jesus. “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me?” (Acts 9:4, BSB)
tags: Saul on the Road to Damascus

content: When Saul asked, “Who are You, Lord?” on the road, who answered?
explanation: Saul met the risen Jesus. “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting” (Acts 9:5, BSB)
tags: Saul on the Road to Damascus

content: After meeting Jesus on the road to Damascus, how long was Saul blind?
explanation: He did not eat or drink. “For three days he was without sight” (Acts 9:9, BSB)
tags: Saul on the Road to Damascus

content: Which disciple in Damascus placed his hands on blind Saul?
explanation: The Lord sent him in a vision. “So Ananias went to the house, and when he arrived, he placed his hands on Saul.” (Acts 9:17, BSB)
tags: Saul on the Road to Damascus

content: When Ananias prayed for Saul in Damascus, what fell from Saul's eyes?
explanation: His sight was restored. “something like scales fell from Saul’s eyes” (Acts 9:18, BSB)
tags: Saul on the Road to Damascus

content: Which king put Peter in prison during the Feast of Unleavened Bread?
explanation: He had already killed James. “He arrested him and put him in prison” (Acts 12:4, BSB)

content: While Herod kept Peter in prison, what was the church doing?
explanation: Prayer was their weapon. “but the church was fervently praying to God for him.” (Acts 12:5, BSB)

content: On the night before his trial under Herod, how was Peter sleeping?
explanation: He was bound with two chains. “Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains” (Acts 12:6, BSB)

content: When the angel woke Peter in Herod's prison, what fell off his wrists?
explanation: God set him free. “And the chains fell off his wrists.” (Acts 12:7, BSB)

content: As the angel led Peter out of prison, how did the iron gate open?
explanation: Nothing could stop God's rescue. “came to the iron gate leading to the city, which opened for them by itself.” (Acts 12:10, BSB)

content: After escaping prison, who answered when Peter knocked at the house gate?
explanation: Many were praying inside. “a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer it.” (Acts 12:13, BSB)

content: When Rhoda heard Peter's voice at the gate, what did she forget to do?
explanation: She was so overjoyed. “she was so overjoyed that she forgot to open the gate” (Acts 12:14, BSB)

content: Who was beaten and thrown into prison with Paul in Philippi?
explanation: The magistrates ordered it. “The crowd joined in the attack against Paul and Silas” (Acts 16:22, BSB)

content: In the Philippian prison, what were Paul's and Silas's feet fastened in?
explanation: They were in the inner cell. “he placed them in the inner cell and fastened their feet in the stocks.” (Acts 16:24, BSB)

content: What were Paul and Silas doing in prison about midnight?
explanation: The other prisoners listened. “About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God” (Acts 16:25, BSB)

content: While Paul and Silas sang in prison, what shook the prison's foundations?
explanation: All the doors flew open. “Suddenly a strong earthquake shook the foundations of the prison.” (Acts 16:26, BSB)

content: When the jailer was about to kill himself, what did Paul shout?
explanation: No prisoner had escaped. “Do not harm yourself! We are all here!” (Acts 16:28, BSB)

content: What did the Philippian jailer ask Paul and Silas?
options: What must I do to be saved?
explanation: He trembled before them. “Sirs, what must I do to be saved?” (Acts 16:30, BSB)

content: What did Paul and Silas tell the jailer he must do to be saved?
explanation: His household could be saved too. “Believe in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved, you and your household.” (Acts 16:31, BSB)

content: To which country was Paul sailing as a prisoner when the great storm struck?
explanation: He was going to stand before Caesar. “When it was decided that we would sail for Italy” (Acts 27:1, BSB)

content: In the great storm on Paul's ship, what did not appear for many days?
explanation: They lost all hope. “When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days” (Acts 27:20, BSB)

content: During the storm at sea, who stood beside Paul in the night?
explanation: He brought a message of hope. “For just last night an angel of God, whose I am and whom I serve, stood beside me” (Acts 27:23, BSB)

content: During the storm, what did Paul say would be the only loss?
explanation: No one would die. “you will not experience any loss of life, but only of the ship.” (Acts 27:22, BSB)

content: When Paul's ship broke up, how many people reached land safely?
explanation: God kept His promise. “In this way everyone was brought safely to land.” (Acts 27:44, BSB)

content: On which island did Paul land after the shipwreck?
explanation: The islanders were very kind. “we learned that the island was called Malta.” (Acts 28:1, BSB)

content: After the shipwreck, what fastened onto Paul's hand by the fire?
explanation: He shook it off and was not hurt. “a viper, driven out by the heat, fastened itself to his hand.” (Acts 28:3, BSB)

content: Who was chosen by lot to replace Judas as an apostle?
explanation: He joined the eleven apostles. “and the lot fell to Matthias; so he was added to the eleven apostles.” (Acts 1:26, BSB)

content: From which mountain did the apostles return after Jesus went up to heaven?
explanation: It is near Jerusalem. “Then they returned to Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives” (Acts 1:12, BSB)

content: After Jesus went up to heaven, where did the apostles stay in Jerusalem?
explanation: They prayed together there. “they went to the upper room where they were staying” (Acts 1:13, BSB)

content: At Pentecost, what did Peter tell the crowd to do?
explanation: They would receive the Holy Spirit. “Repent and be baptized, every one of you” (Acts 2:38, BSB)

content: Peter said salvation is found in no other name except whose?
explanation: Peter was speaking of Jesus Christ of Nazareth. “Salvation exists in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given to men by which we must be saved.” (Acts 4:12, BSB)

content: The leaders saw Peter and John were ordinary men but noticed they had been with whom?
explanation: Time with Jesus made them bold. “and took note that these men had been with Jesus.” (Acts 4:13, BSB)

content: What does the name Barnabas mean?
explanation: The apostles gave him this name. “whom the apostles called Barnabas (meaning Son of Encouragement)” (Acts 4:36, BSB)

content: By secretly keeping back money from the land, whom did Peter say Ananias had lied to?
explanation: Lying to the church was lying to God. “how is it that Satan has filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit” (Acts 5:3, BSB)

content: How did Saul's disciples help him escape from Damascus?
explanation: They let him down through the wall. “lowered him in a basket through a window in the wall.” (Acts 9:25, BSB)

content: In which city were believers in Jesus first given the name Christians?
explanation: Barnabas and Saul taught there a year. “The disciples were first called Christians at Antioch.” (Acts 11:26, BSB)

content: By what other name was Saul also called?
explanation: He is best known by this name. “Then Saul, who was also called Paul” (Acts 13:9, BSB)

content: Who was Cornelius, the God-fearing man in Caesarea?
explanation: He was in the Italian Regiment. “a man named Cornelius, a centurion in what was called the Italian Regiment.” (Acts 10:1, BSB)

content: In Peter's vision of the sheet, what did the voice say about what God made clean?
explanation: God welcomes all nations. “Do not call anything impure that God has made clean.” (Acts 10:15, BSB)

content: At Cornelius's house, what did Peter say he now truly understood about God?
explanation: God welcomes every nation. “I now truly understand that God does not show favoritism” (Acts 10:34, BSB)

content: Which apostle did King Herod put to death with the sword?
explanation: Then Herod arrested Peter. “He had James, the brother of John, put to death with the sword.” (Acts 12:2, BSB)

content: When Rhoda said Peter was at the gate, what did the praying believers say?
options: You are out of your mind
explanation: They found it hard to believe. ““You are out of your mind,” they told her.” (Acts 12:15, BSB)

content: After parting with Barnabas, whom did Paul choose as his new partner?
explanation: Barnabas took Mark to Cyprus. “but Paul chose Silas and left” (Acts 15:40, BSB)

content: In Philippi, what did Lydia sell?
explanation: The Lord opened her heart. “a woman named Lydia, a dealer in purple cloth” (Acts 16:14, BSB)

content: After believing, what did the Philippian jailer do for Paul and Silas that night?
explanation: Then he and his household were baptized. “At that hour of the night, the jailer took them and washed their wounds.” (Acts 16:33, BSB)

content: In Athens, what was written on the altar Paul found?
explanation: Paul told them about the true God. “TO AN UNKNOWN GOD.” (Acts 17:23, BSB)

content: What trade did Paul share with Aquila and Priscilla?
explanation: He worked to support himself. “because they were tentmakers by trade, just as he was.” (Acts 18:3, BSB)

content: Which young man fell asleep and fell from a window while Paul preached?
explanation: Paul talked on and on. “a certain young man named Eutychus, seated in the window, was sinking into a deep sleep” (Acts 20:9, BSB)

content: Paul quoted the Lord Jesus: it is more blessed to give than to do what?
explanation: We must help the weak. “It is more blessed to give than to receive.” (Acts 20:35, BSB)

content: On Malta, what did Paul do with the viper that bit his hand?
options: Shook it off into the fire
explanation: He suffered no harm. “But Paul shook the creature off into the fire and suffered no ill effects.” (Acts 28:5, BSB)

content: How did Paul live during his two years in Rome?
explanation: He welcomed all who came. “Paul stayed there two full years in his own rented house” (Acts 28:30, BSB)

content: About how many believers were gathered when Peter stood up to choose Judas's replacement?
explanation: They were waiting in Jerusalem. “(a gathering of about a hundred and twenty)” (Acts 1:15, BSB)

content: Besides Matthias, who was the other man proposed to replace Judas?
explanation: He was also known as Justus. “Joseph called Barsabbas (also known as Justus) and Matthias.” (Acts 1:23, BSB)

content: At what hour of prayer did Peter and John go up to the temple and heal the lame man?
explanation: It was afternoon. “at the hour of prayer, the ninth hour.” (Acts 3:1, BSB)

content: After the lame man was healed, where did the astonished people run to Peter and John?
explanation: Peter then preached to them. “the walkway called Solomon’s Colonnade.” (Acts 3:11, BSB)

content: Barnabas was a Levite from which island?
explanation: He later sailed back there. “Joseph, a Levite from Cyprus” (Acts 4:36, BSB)

content: The Ethiopian official was in charge of the treasury of which queen?
explanation: She was queen of the Ethiopians. “in charge of the entire treasury of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians.” (Acts 8:27, BSB)

content: On which street in Damascus was Saul staying when Ananias came?
explanation: He was at the house of Judas. “Go to the house of Judas on Straight Street” (Acts 9:11, BSB)

content: Saul of the Damascus road came from which city?
explanation: The Lord named it to Ananias. “a man from Tarsus named Saul” (Acts 9:11, BSB)

content: How many squads of soldiers did Herod use to guard Peter in prison?
explanation: Herod wanted no escape. “handing him over to be guarded by four squads of four soldiers each.” (Acts 12:4, BSB)

content: After escaping prison, Peter went to the house of Mary, the mother of whom?
explanation: Many were praying there. “he went to the house of Mary the mother of John, also called Mark” (Acts 12:12, BSB)

content: In Lystra, the crowd called Paul Hermes. What did they call Barnabas?
explanation: Paul was the chief speaker. “Barnabas they called Zeus, and Paul they called Hermes” (Acts 14:12, BSB)

content: Lydia, the seller of purple cloth, came from which city?
explanation: She listened to Paul in Philippi. “a dealer in purple cloth from the city of Thyatira” (Acts 16:14, BSB)

content: How many people were on board Paul's ship before the shipwreck?
explanation: All of them reached land. “In all, there were 276 of us on board.” (Acts 27:37, BSB)

content: What was the name of the centurion who guarded Paul on the voyage to Italy?
explanation: He belonged to the Imperial Regiment. “were handed over to a centurion named Julius” (Acts 27:1, BSB)

content: In Ephesus, what did former magicians burn in front of everyone?
explanation: They were worth fifty thousand drachmas. “brought their books and burned them in front of everyone.” (Acts 19:19, BSB)

content: Which king asked Paul, “Can you persuade me in such a short time to become a Christian?”
explanation: Paul was on trial before him. “Then Agrippa said to Paul” (Acts 26:28, BSB)
